beats.trigger: ## Multi-Agent Systems
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Hire three agents to search. Three more to decide. The filesystem is the meeting room.
beats.got: Something about many agents and files. I don't know what a meeting room has to do with it.

beats.trigger: [Schedule your personal agent](exercises/personal-agent-homework.md) to read your challenge memory for a week.
beats.got: Homework before the class. I did not do it.

beats.trigger: **Analyze** handoff failures: hidden conflicts, clashing dialects, beige averaging
beats.got: Nothing. A list of words I don't know. Beige averaging?

beats.trigger: Three agents search Confluence, OneDrive and practitioner articles, and three more decide what it means.
beats.got: Agents search company files. At least that is something I can picture.

beats.trigger: Writing a file changes your folder. Slack changes another system.
beats.got: The agent writes a message and waits for approval before sending. Good, that I understand. It could post a delay notice to the depots.

beats.trigger: Ask the agent to read Module 2's `memory/` and name the **crux**, Richard Rumelt's term for the one thing that, if solved, releases pressure on everything else.
beats.got: The agent finds the one main problem. Fine, but this is a strategy word and I don't have a Module 2 memory to read. Hands-on, yes, but the topic feels like a consultant's.

beats.trigger: Three retrievers fetch raw material on your challenge into `sources/`; a fourth session curates it into `memory/`.
beats.got: Several agents pull material from wiki and docs at the same time and one puts it together. If the material were delivery reports it would be useful. But 28 minutes and four sessions is a lot of windows.

beats.trigger: Spawn three helpers with different stances on your curated memory.
beats.got: Three helpers argue from different angles and then one answer comes out. I don't know why I would want that for a depot plan.

beats.trigger: Two ways to split an agent: three retrievers in separate windows, three stances inside one session.
beats.got: Nothing new. Two ways to split work.

beats.trigger: Build one agent per recurring workflow: a single `.md` file, guardrailed for that job.
beats.got: One agent for each job that repeats. A weekly report is exactly that kind of job.

beats.trigger: If one agent can produce what you need, use one.
beats.got: Start with one agent. Finally something simple and sensible. I like that.

beats.trigger: A legal-policy agent shouldn't have customer-data access.
beats.got: Split when the data access is different. Like the one person who can see payroll and the others who can't. That is clear.

beats.trigger: More input does not fix a beige answer.
beats.got: More agents is not better. Same message as before.

beats.trigger: Hand the synthesizer the strategy kernel (diagnosis, guiding policy, coherent actions).
beats.got: Nothing new. Strategy kernel, no example, I stopped reading.

beats.trigger: Could one prompt produce the same quality of output? If yes, write that one prompt.
beats.got: A simple test before building anything big. I can use that for any idea someone brings me.

beats.trigger: **Helper agents in one session (the Phase 2 move).**
beats.got: Sessions or helpers, I'm not sure which is which. Phase 1, Phase 2, I lost track.

beats.trigger: One agent can call another for a different stance, source zone, or working style.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: A retriever finds two numbers and the curator keeps one.
beats.got: Work gets lost at the handoff between agents. Same as between two depots at shift change. I know that one.

beats.trigger: If one well-prompted agent does the job, write that prompt.
beats.got: Third time it says use one agent if it is enough. OK, I got it.

beats.trigger: Agents get stuck: wrong source, three views averaged into mush, the wrong file written, confident right before a failed handoff.
beats.got: Agents make mistakes, also confident ones. Not a surprise.

beats.trigger: Prompt your stuck system to diagnose whether the bug lives in the sources, the processing, or the boundary between agents.
beats.got: Ask the agent where the problem is before fixing it. Like asking where the truck is before calling the driver.

beats.trigger: Write down the lesson: add a rule to CLAUDE.md: what to read first, what not to smooth over, which output format to produce, when to stop and ask.
beats.got: Write the lesson into a rules file so it doesn't repeat. Same as a depot instruction after an incident.

beats.trigger: Five minutes. The agent reviews the four prompts, the retrieval files, the synthesizer's briefing and the conversation, then rewrites CLAUDE.md in place and reports what changed.
beats.got: The agent reviews its own work and updates the rules file. Fine, but I would not know if it was good.

beats.trigger: The audit reads how your agents handed work to each other. It does not check whether the briefing is true.
beats.got: The review checks the process, not whether the answer is correct. Honest. So I still have to check the numbers myself.

beats.trigger: Push back where the summary is wrong
beats.got: If the summary is wrong, tell it. Like with the depot names in my table.

beats.trigger: The synthesized briefing's correctness stays an open question today.
beats.got: We finish without knowing if the answer is right. I don't like that.

beats.trigger: **Optional move: pressure-test the memory.**
beats.got: Optional, so I skip it.

beats.trigger: Split only where agents can't be one: access, dialect, stance.
beats.got: Short and clear. Split only for a reason.

beats.trigger: [Agent Trigger List, After Module 3]
beats.got: More reading. No.

beats.trigger: Agents add non-deterministic behaviour, prompt injection (direct, or inside retrieved text) and emergent capability you can only bound.
beats.got: nothing new. Long English text, I stopped.

beats.trigger: An agent that works across connected systems has access to those systems.
beats.got: If an agent can get into our systems, I need to know what it could break. That question I would ask IT.

beats.trigger: keep working on your real problem: add an agent for a critical dependency, or a plan visualisation.
beats.got: Keep working on a real problem. I don't have time for it.

take_homes: Start with one agent. Split only if there is a real reason, like different access.
Work gets lost at the handoffs between agents, like at a shift change. Check there.
The agent's review checks the process, not whether the answer is true. I still check the numbers.

misconception.why: I saw agents read company files and put the material together. So it is not only a chatbot for customers. But I did not see it do anything with operations data, so I am not convinced yet.

one_line: Use one agent, not many, check the handoffs, but too many strategy words and I did not see my own work in it.
